verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 17.35
4. Catutthavagga
Acirapakkantasutta
Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate acirapakkante devadatte.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain, not long after Devadatta had left.

verses.pali: Tatra kho bhagavā devadattaṁ ārabbha bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: There the Buddha spoke to the mendicants about Devadatta:

verses.pali: “attavadhāya, bhikkhave, devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi, parābhavāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi.
verses.english: “Possessions, honor, and popularity came to Devadatta for his own ruin and downfall.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kadalī attavadhāya phalaṁ deti, parābhavāya phalaṁ deti;
evameva kho, bhikkhave, attavadhāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi, parābhavāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi.
Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, veḷu attavadhāya phalaṁ deti, parābhavāya phalaṁ deti;
evameva kho, bhikkhave, attavadhāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi, parābhavāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi.
Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, naḷo attavadhāya phalaṁ deti, parābhavāya phalaṁ deti;
verses.english: or a reed, all of which bear fruit to their own ruin and downfall …

verses.pali: evameva kho, bhikkhave, attavadhāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi, parābhavāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi.
Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, assatarī attavadhāya gabbhaṁ gaṇhāti, parābhavāya gabbhaṁ gaṇhāti;
verses.english: It’s like a mule, which becomes pregnant to its own ruin and downfall.

verses.pali: evameva kho, bhikkhave, attavadhāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi, parābhavāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi.
verses.english: In the same way, possessions, honor, and popularity came to Devadatta for his own ruin and downfall.

verses.pali: Evaṁ dāruṇo kho, bhikkhave, lābhasakkārasiloko.
verses.english: So grim are possessions, honor, and popularity.

verses.pali: Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabban”ti.
Idamavoca bhagavā.
verses.english: That is what the Buddha said.

verses.pali: Idaṁ vatvāna sugato athāparaṁ etadavoca satthā:
verses.english: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:

verses.pali: “Phalaṁ ve kadaliṁ hanti,
verses.english: “The banana plant is destroyed by its own fruit,

verses.pali: phalaṁ veḷuṁ phalaṁ naḷaṁ;
verses.english: as are the bamboo and the reed.

verses.pali: Sakkāro kāpurisaṁ hanti,
gabbho assatariṁ yathā”ti.
Pañcamaṁ.
